name: אִישׁ־בֹּשֶׁת
summary: Saul’s son, whom Abner made king over Israel at Mahanaim after Saul’s death while Judah followed David (2Sa 2:8–10). He reigned two years, lost Abner after charging him over Saul’s concubine (2Sa 3:7–10), gave Michal back to David (2Sa 3:14–15), and was murdered on his bed by Rechab and Baanah, whom David put to death for it (2Sa 4:5–12). The name is אִישׁ “man of” and בֹּשֶׁת “shame”. Chronicles gives the same son of Saul as אֶשְׁבַּעַל (1Ch 8:33; 9:39), so בֹּשֶׁת stands where that name has בַּעַל, as יְרֻבֶּשֶׁת stands for Jerubbaal (2Sa 11:21; Jdg 7:1) and Mephibosheth for Merib-baal (2Sa 4:4; 1Ch 8:34). The prophets use בֹּשֶׁת in the same way as a name for Baal (Hos 9:10; Jer 11:13), and Yahweh says he will take the names of the Baals out of Israel’s mouth (Hos 2:19).

evidence.note: “Abner son of Ner, commander of Saul’s army, took אִישׁ בֹּשֶׁת son of Saul and brought him over to Mahanaim.”
Forty years old when he became king over Israel, and he reigned two years; the house of Judah followed David.
Twelve “for Benjamin and for Ish-bosheth son of Saul” against twelve of David’s servants at Gibeon.
He charges Abner over Rizpah, and Abner’s anger burns “at the words of Ish-bosheth”.
David sends to him for Michal, and he takes her from her husband (מֵעִם אִישׁ) Paltiel.
Rechab and Baanah kill him on his bed at noon and bring his head to David at Hebron.
David calls him “a righteous man (אִישׁ־צַדִּיק) in his own house on his bed”, puts the murderers to death, and buries his head in Abner’s grave.
The same son of Saul under the name אֶשְׁבַּעַל: בֹּשֶׁת answers to בַּעַל.
“Abimelech son of יְרֻבֶּשֶׁת”: Jerubbaal (Jdg 7:1) with בֶּשֶׁת for בַּעַל.
Jonathan’s son מְפִיבֹשֶׁת, who is מְרִיב בַּעַל in 1Ch 8:34.
“They came to Baal-peor and separated themselves לַבֹּשֶׁת, to the shame.”
“Altars לַבֹּשֶׁת, to the shame, altars to burn incense to the Baal”: the two are one.
“I will take the names of the Baals out of her mouth, and they shall be remembered by their name no more.”

note: The brief’s 17 tokens for a.da.ac are counted by the spelling בֹּשֶׁת, so they include the common noun “shame” (Jer 7:19; Hab 2:10; Zep 3:5; Psa 132:18; Dan 9:7–8); the name’s own verses are 2Sa 2:8, 10, 12, 15; 3:8, 14, 15; 4:5, 8 (twice), 12. The text writes the name both with maqqef (אִישׁ־בֹּשֶׁת, 2Sa 2:10) and without (אִישׁ בֹּשֶׁת, 2Sa 2:8). That בֹּשֶׁת replaces בַּעַל is shown from the paired names in scripture; who made the change, and when, the text does not say. The second element belongs to the root בוש, which has no entry yet. Saul’s son יִשְׁוִי (1Sa 14:49) is a separate TIPNR person (a form of Abinadab@1Sa.14.49) and is not identified with Ish-bosheth here. See also names/eshbaal.
